title: Coefficient enlargement of the explicit completed tensor component
statement: Fix l,X,R,closed,models, symmetry, a finite-model family N and signed tensor coherence as in lem-sf-adic-completed-tensor-common-component-naturality. For any common-stage objects P,Q and any finite field E containing their two fields, the explicit completedTensorCommonComponent(P,Q) equals the completedTensorStageComponent at E of P.toStage and Q.toStage conjugated by the actual isoToStage maps, with the closed tensor of ordinary realizations on the source and realized common-stage tensor on the target. This is an equality of objectwise component formulas, without any input morphisms.

source.place: BS Definition 3.4.10 and Remark 6.8.15; HRS Proposition 5.2 and Lemma 7.9; the corresponding part of the finite normalized realization argument.

proof.text: At the coefficient compositum E0, unfold the common component. Identify the existing natural inclusion tensor comparison with stageTensor using its uniquely normalized formula, functoriality of mapIso and associativity. Thus the common component is the conjugate of the finite stage component at E0.

The two input fields lie in the requested field E, so their compositum E0 lies in E. Apply the finite scalar square to the pair at E0 and its extension to E. Apply fixed-stage naturality at E to the two scalar associators, correcting the double extension to the direct extension of the original objects.

The stage-system cocycle shows that isoToStage to E0, then isoToStage to E, then the included scalar associator is exactly isoToStage directly to E, in both coordinates. Compose the two squares, map the isomorphism identities through the two functors, and cancel the adjacent inverse maps. This gives the claimed conjugation formula.

proof_origin.place: BS Definition 3.4.10 and Remark 6.8.15; HRS Proposition 5.2 and Lemma 7.9; the corresponding part of the finite normalized realization argument.
proof_origin.note: U9: explicit compositum transport and scalar-associator correction, combined by functorial conjugation; the two-field scalar square is a separate strictly finite-source normalization step.

theorem completedTensorCommonComponent_stage_transport
    (symmetry : @SymmetricCategory _ _ closed.monoidal)
    (N : ∀ E, CompletedTensorFiniteModel l X R closed models E)
    (coherence : RingedDerivedTensorCoherence.{u + 1, u, u + 1}
      (ProEt.topology X) (ring l X R) closed models symmetry)
    (P Q : generalAlgebraicallyClosedConstructibleCategory l (PadicAlgCl l) X)
    (E : AlgebraicallyClosedCoefficients.Index l (PadicAlgCl l))
    (hP : P.stage ≤ E) (hQ : Q.stage ≤ E) :
    let a := (GeneralAlgebraicallyClosedCoefficients.stageSystem l
      (PadicAlgCl l) X).isoToStage P hP
    let b := (GeneralAlgebraicallyClosedCoefficients.stageSystem l
      (PadicAlgCl l) X).isoToStage Q hQ
    (completedTensorCommonComponent l X R closed models N P Q).hom =
      (((ordinary l X R).prod (ordinary l X R)) ⋙ closed.tensor).map
          (Prod.mkHom a.hom b.hom) ≫
        (completedTensorStageComponent l X R closed models E (N E)
          (P.toStage hP) (Q.toStage hQ)).hom ≫
        (commonStageDerivedTensor l (PadicAlgCl l) X ⋙ ordinary l X R).map
          (Prod.mkHom a.inv b.inv)
